newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt envoy returns to Israel for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt envoy returns to Israel for peace talks.

text.p: The senior adviser of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak will meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday as part of efforts to break the deadlock in the Middle East peace process.
The office of Osama el-Baz said he had left for Tel Aviv on his second visit to the Jewish state in 48 hours.
Baz flew to Israel on Friday to meet Netanyahu and pave the way for a summit meeting between the Israeli leader and Mubarak in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh on Tuesday.
Palestinian-Israeli talks ground to a halt two months ago when Netanyahu approved the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in 1967.

Egypt, which considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the peace talks, backs the Palestinian demand for halting settlement activity before the talks resume. But on Saturday, Mubarak said Baz would meet Netanyahu to try to revive the peace talks without any preconditions.

"We have not talked about conditions, we are talking about how to solve the present crisis, we cannot say preconditions," Mubarak told a news conference after meeting Jordan's King Hussein, who is also trying to break the deadlock.
Mubarak it was too early to talk about an Egyptian initiative to revive the talks but he has suggested a six-month Israeli freeze of settlement activity to boost peace efforts.
Israel reaffirmed its stand ahead of Tuesday's summit, with Israeli Cabinet Minister Danny Naveh saying the Jewish state would continue building the controversial settlement.
